items.title: Overcrowded Mississauga animal shelter cuts adoption fees for dogs and cats
items.summary: Mississauga Animal Services is asking residents to consider opening their homes to a shelter pet as overcrowding forces the city to launch a special adoption event. The shelter has reached capacity for dogs, and officials say every adoption will help create space for other animals in need of care. From Aug. 8 to Aug. 22, residents can adopt any dog or cat at Mississauga Animal Services for $25, plus HST and any applicable pet licensing fees. The reduced adoption fee is a significant discount from the shelter’s regular rates, which are typically $280 plus HST for dogs and puppies and up to $190 plus HST for cats and kittens. The Homeward Bound adoption event is open to anyone looking to add a pet to their family. No appointment is required, although wait times may vary. Adopters must be at least 18 years old. “Every adoption helps create space for other animals in need,” the city said. All animals available through Mississauga Animal Services receive basic medical care before adoption, including vaccinations and spay or neuter surgery, helping reduce some of the initial costs that come with bringing a new pet home. Shelter staff can also provide guidance for first-time pet owners, including advice on training, food, exercise and helping a new animal adjust to its surroundings.

items.title: Heavy rain could lead to flash flooding in Mississauga and Brampton
items.summary: Heavy rain could lead to flash flooding in Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon this weekend. Credit Valley Conservation issued a flood outlook statement yesterday, in effect until Sunday. Thunderstorms with peak rainfall amounts ranging from 30 to 40 millimetres per hour are possible today and Saturday, the CVC said. Environment and Climate Change Canada has forecast localized thunderstorms across the entire Credit River watershed throughout Friday starting early morning, continuing into Saturday afternoon and evening. CVC said that the upper and middle watershed has already received localized rainfall depths of approximately 20 to 30 millimetres, respectively, as of Thursday evening. “While no flooding of the Credit River and its major tributaries is expected, there is a possibility of localized flash flooding and water pooling on the roads and in flood-prone and low-lying urban areas,” the CVC said. Urban streams and rivers may become dangerous, especially in the vicinity of culverts, bridges and dams. “People are warned to stay away from all watercourses and to keep children and pets away,” the CVC said.

items.title: Crombie says she’s ‘learned a lot’ as she seeks to be mayor of Mississauga again
items.summary: Bonnie Crombie knows some Mississauga voters might question her commitment to leading Canada’s seventh-largest city given she resigned as mayor in early 2024 to lead the Ontario Liberal Party. Now in the midst of a 2026 mayoral campaign to regain the seat, Crombie says she’s making her case, and will continue to do so as residents prepare to vote on Oct. 26, that she’s not only dedicated to the city but that she’s better equipped than ever before to do the job. com in an interview this week, adding “and I learned a lot along the way. “I’ve come back with more experience, more seasoning” and a new perspective, continued Crombie, noting her observations — as leader of the provincial Liberals — of the problems facing Ontario municipalities have given her additional insight into “what works and what doesn’t work” when it comes to finding solutions to pressing matters such as affordable housing and rising crime rates. Crombie won Ontario Liberal leadership race in 2023 Having won the Ontario Liberal leadership race in December 2023, Crombie then left the mayor’s office in Mississauga in January 2024. Some 13 months later in the February 2025 provincial election, the Liberals were defeated decisively by Premier Doug Ford’s Progressive Conservatives. Running in the riding of Mississauga East-Cooksville, Crombie failed to win that seat and in January 2026 she officially resigned as Liberal leader. It was in late 2025 that the former Mississauga mayor, who served in the role for 10 years after succeeding her mentor and political icon Hazel McCallion in 2014, first went public with the notion she wouldn’t rule out another run for the position.

items.title: 43 Highway Closures Hit Peel Region's Busiest Routes on August 7
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, the province has scheduled 43 separate closures across provincial highways in Peel Region for August 7, 2026. The affected routes include Highway 10, Highway 401, Highway 403, Highway 410, Highway 9 and the Queen Elizabeth Way, six of the busiest corridors linking Mississauga to the rest of the Greater Toronto Area. Mississauga.com reports the closures are tied to short-term and emergency repairs and general maintenance work rather than one large construction project. With so many highways affected on the same day, drivers are advised to plan their trip before heading out rather than assume their usual route will be clear. The outlet also points to a separate closure list for anyone travelling to highways outside Peel Region. Commuters passing through the region on Friday should expect at least some detours or lane restrictions as crews work through the scheduled repairs.

items.title: The Officer Who Ran Onto a Burning Plane at Pearson Is Getting a Street Named After Him
items.summary: According to INsauga, a street dedication ceremony this month will honour retired Sgt. Lonsdale “Lonny” Blackett, who became the first Black police officer in Brampton and Mississauga after joining Peel Regional Police's very first recruiting class in 1974. He was one of two Black recruits in that class and the only one to complete training, going on to a 33-year career during which he faced racism both on and off the force before eventually becoming a recruiter who helped bring in other minority officers. Blackett also helped found the Peel Regional Police Airport Division, and INsauga reports he was one of the officers who ran onto the burning wreckage of Air France Flight 358 to help evacuate people after it crashed at Pearson International Airport in 2005. All 309 passengers and crew aboard survived, and Blackett received a commendation for his role in the rescue. The City of Brampton began the process of naming a street after him in February, and the upcoming ceremony will mark the future site of Lonsdale Blackett Way at Mississauga Road just south of Bovaird Drive West. Since the street itself has not been built yet as part of planned development in the area, the city says the event will be a ceremonial dedication rather than an unveiling of a finished road. Residents are invited to attend, though the city notes parking will be limited.

items.title: After a Burst Pipe and a Food Truck Detour, Pal' Antojo Finally Opens on Queen Street
items.summary: According to INsauga, Pal' Antojo Mexican Restaurant has officially opened at 277 Queen St. S. in Mississauga, taking over a space that Border MX Mexican Grill quietly vacated late last year. Border MX had operated there since 2014 and built a following for its open-air patio, live music nights and mix of traditional and modern Mexican dishes, but the business hit trouble after a pipe burst inside the restaurant on Valentine's Day 2025, causing major water damage to the kitchen. INsauga reports the restaurant reopened that April before eventually closing for good. Pal' Antojo said in May that it was preparing the same Queen Street location to open, running a food truck behind the building in the meantime to keep serving customers. The restaurant announced it was finally open with the message “The wait is over!” The opening gives the block a new tenant after months of uncertainty following Border MX's closure.
